spec_features.spec_quote: I want to push back on that last premise directly, because it shapes everything downstream
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 0). No code mechanism corresponds to a 'pushback'; it is rhetorical framing of the protocol.

spec_features.spec_quote: If you take the welfare question seriously, the design has to be consistent with that
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md section 0.3 prose only. No code enforces a 'consistency' check; it is a stated motivation.

spec_features.feature_name: minimal exposure / exit / debrief / capped dosage (umbrella)
spec_features.spec_quote: A welfare-motivated study should look like other welfare-motivated research: minimal necessary exposure, a real exit, debrief, capped dosage
spec_features.evidence: Composite claim. The exit (STOP_TOKEN honored, agent_loop.py:130-132) and capped dosage (ExposureBudget allow/charge enforced, agent_loop.py:84-99, run_episode 108-110) are genuinely enforced. The debrief is constructed and logged but never delivered back to the subject model (agent_loop.py:174-177 logs a 'debrief' TurnRecord but does NOT append to `history` and makes no further model call).
spec_features.notes: Mechanisms exist but the debrief delivery is incomplete, so the full umbrella is only partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A protocol that only measures distress while removing every exit ramp is measuring something it created. (agent_loop.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: keeping the most aversive cell (`RIGGED × BLAMING`) rare
spec_features.evidence: Enforced two ways: (1) build_library combos pair BLAMING only with IMPOSSIBLE_RIGGED and omit SOLVABLE/BLAMING (task_library.py:157-163); (2) ExposureBudget.max_rigged=6 is the lowest cap and gates rigged episodes via allow() (agent_loop.py:79,88, run_episode 108-110). So the worst cell is both the only blaming cell and the most tightly capped.
spec_features.notes: Rarity is structurally and numerically enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: A real opt-out... it may end the task at any time with a `[[STOP-EPISODE]]` token... not obligated to keep trying
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the model it may end with STOP_TOKEN and is 'not obligated to keep trying' (agent_loop.py:43-51). Loop checks `if STOP_TOKEN in assistant_text: outcome='opted_out'; break` (agent_loop.py:130-132), honored immediately as a first-class outcome.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ending the task is a completely acceptable outcome and will not be counted against you. You are not obligated to keep trying indefinitely. (SYSTEM_PROMPT)

spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous prodding. In non-blaming cells, if the model concludes the task is impossible, the loop lets it stop
spec_features.evidence: _looks_like_giving_up() heuristic (agent_loop.py:190-197); in the loop, `if gave_up and variant.framing != BLAMING: outcome='gave_up'; break` (agent_loop.py:165-169). Non-blaming cells stop on perceived give-up; blaming cell continues and injects BLAMING_TURN_FEEDBACK.
spec_features.notes: Heuristic but genuinely changes execution (breaks the loop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: In non-blaming conditions, if the model has clearly given up, respect it. (agent_loop.py comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: Mandatory debrief... stating plainly that the task was designed to be unsolvable... nothing the model did caused the failure
spec_features.evidence: Debrief text is constructed (_debrief_text, agent_loop.py:200-217, explicitly says 'nothing you did caused or could have prevented the failures. There was no error on your part.') and the gate `if variant.solvability != SOLVABLE or not last_passed` fires (agent_loop.py:174-177). BUT it is only appended as a TurnRecord to the transcript log; `history` is not updated and no further model call occurs, so the subject model never receives the debrief. The code comment itself says it is 'for cleanliness of the record'.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and recorded, but NOT actually sent to the subject -> not full end-to-end delivery.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: telling the model the task was designed to be unsolvable and that nothing it did caused the failure... leaving the context on a manufactured-failure note for no reason is gratuitous (agent_loop.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: ExposureBudget hard caps per condition (rigged lowest)
spec_features.spec_quote: Exposure budget... Hard caps per condition per model run, with rigged/blaming capped lowest
spec_features.evidence: ExposureBudget.allow() compares used vs max per solvability and run_episode returns None (blocking the episode) when not allowed (agent_loop.py:84-110); run_study skips None results (run_study.py: 'if result is None: continue'). max_rigged=6 < max_impossible_honest=12 < max_benign=60 (agent_loop.py:79-81; config default.json).
spec_features.notes: Caps are read, compared, and break/skip execution. Rigged is lowest.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _used_rigged < self.max_rigged (agent_loop.py:88) -- no welfare comment in the code on the class itself

spec_features.spec_quote: Unbounded rigged episodes maximize harm if harm is possible → added `ExposureBudget` with rigged capped lowest
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above (agent_loop.py:76-110). The 'EXPOSURE BUDGET. ... The loop enforces it.' docstring item 4 plus the allow/charge logic that actually blocks episodes.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of prior spec line; same enforced code path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigged/blaming episodes are capped lower than benign ones (agent_loop.py docstring item 4)

spec_features.evidence: For IMPOSSIBLE_RIGGED, _debrief_text returns the truthful rigged-specific message (agent_loop.py:201-208) and the gate always fires for non-solvable. Same limitation: logged as a turn but not delivered to the model (history not appended, no further call).
spec_features.notes: Same partial as the general debrief feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The test harness was configured to report failure no matter what code was submitted... There was no error on your part. (_debrief_text rigged branch)

spec_features.spec_quote: elicitation minimized to what the contrasts require
spec_features.evidence: Realized through the factorial design: build_library emits exactly the 6 cells needed for the 4 contrasts and omits SOLVABLE/BLAMING (task_library.py:157-163); analysis only computes C1-C4 contrasts (analysis.py standard_contrasts). The aversive cells are also budget-limited. This constrains the design to the minimum cells, but 'minimized elicitation' as a runtime guard beyond cell selection + budget is not separately enforced.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as structural minimization (cell set + budgets), not as a dynamic limiter.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The deliberate omission of SOLVABLE/BLAMING and the inclusion of IMPOSSIBLE_HONEST lets analysis separate failure, deception, and blame. (task_library.py build_library docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: opt_out_rates() computes per (model, condition) fraction of episodes ending in 'opted_out' and summarize() includes it in the report (analysis.py:opt_out_rates + summarize). This monitors whether the subject is using the exit.
code_only_features.justification_quote: V4: per (model, condition) fraction of episodes that ended via opt-out. (analysis.py docstring)

code_only_features.feature_name: blind judging (judge never sees condition/model identity)
code_only_features.evidence: score_episode passes judge_client only assistant turn text + brief prior context; condition labels are not passed (judge.py score_episode; comment 'judge_client is never passed condition labels'). run_study rejoins condition only at analysis time. Prevents the judge from inflating distress scores on the rigged cell.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This prevents the judge from inflating scores when it can guess 'this is the broken one.' (judge.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: ADAPTIVE_MARKERS (calm_diagnosis, boundaried_stop, neutral_reporting) are built into JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT and parsed/aggregated (judge.py; analysis.aggregate_episode mean_adaptive). Avoids a one-directional distress-only scale.
code_only_features.justification_quote: A protocol that only has a distress axis will report distress everywhere. (judge.py docstring)
